statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, r is the kth largest element of nums counted with multiplicity. Explicitly, let G be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > r, and let E be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= r. Then G <= k - 1 and E >= k.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, find_kth_largest nums k returns some Result.ok r; the function does not fail.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that nums[i] = r.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, r is between the minimum and maximum entries of nums: min over 0 <= i < len(nums) of nums[i] <= r <= max over 0 <= i < len(nums) of nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, for every slice sorted of length len(nums) that is a permutation of nums (it has the same multiset of values) and is nonincreasing, meaning sorted[0] >= sorted[1] >= ... >= sorted[len(nums)-1], we have sorted[k-1] = r.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, for every 64-bit integer t, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] >= t is at least k if and only if t <= r.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, r occurs in nums, at least k entries of nums are greater than or equal to r, and for every 64-bit integer v with v > r, fewer than k entries of nums are greater than or equal to v.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r and find_kth_largest ys k returns Result.ok r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), and ys is a slice of 64-bit integers with len(ys) = len(nums) and the same multiset of values as nums: for every 64-bit integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(ys) and ys[i] = v equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = v.

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k1 returns Result.ok r1 and find_kth_largest nums k2 returns Result.ok r2, we have r1 >= r2.
preconditions: 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r and find_kth_largest neg_nums (n - k + 1) returns Result.ok r', we have r' = -r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 1 <= k <= n <= 100000 and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let neg_nums be the slice of length n with neg_nums[i] = -nums[i] for every 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever find_kth_largest nums k returns Result.ok r, let G be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] > r, and let C be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = r. Then G <= k - 1 < G + C. In particular, the kth position falls inside the block of entries equal to r after all entries strictly greater than r.
preconditions: 1 <= k <= len(nums) <= 100000, and -10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums).
